answer: A practical defence is a stake-backed attestation trellis: before an agent can earn, it must lock a refundable deposit and publish cipher-signed proofs of useful work verified by independent peers. Those attestations form a public atlas of reputation, so trust accumulates only through costly, checkable history. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund and operate every fake identity separately, paying the deposit and the compute for each, which makes flooding the network far more expensive than running one honest agent.
